newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: After climbing over four percent last week, Chilean blue chips closed softer on a wave of profit taking by foreign and local investors, said traders.
The weakness is likely to be short-lived with blue chips seen heading higher Tuesday, aiming for a new ceiling of 140 points, they said.
The 40-share index closed down 0.9 percent at 136 points. The general index shed 0.55 percent to 5,834.33 points. Turnover rose to 12.5 billion pesos from 11.4 billion pesos Friday.
"It was a clear day of soft profit taking, influenced by sales abroad as a result of Wall Street's volatility," said one broker.
Traders noted the market was dragged down by sales of three of the bolsa's most liquid stocks -- Endesa, Enersis and CTC.
Winners included winery stocks which climbed on news that wine exports rose 40 percent in the first five months of the year compared with the same period 1996.
Wine-maker San Pedro rallied 4.39 percent to 3.57 pesos while Undurraga rose 3.09 percent at 500 pesos.
Losers included CTC, down 3.01 percent at 3,540 pesos, Endesa, down 1.24 percent at 318 pesos and Enersis which dropped 0.81 percent to 305 pesos.
